Most of the packet is student recognition, running alphabetically from All-State winter athletes through the WordMasters Challenge. The business agenda awards the Administration and Services building roof replacement to J.D. Candler Roofing for $341,400.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, renews the Sodexo Management, Inc. food service contract, buys a food service point-of-sale system from Business Machine Company for $37,401.00, and raises paid lunch prices by $0.15.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, Tuesday, June 2, 2015, 7:00 p.m., at Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085. District offices: 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition (Item 2, A through HHH)**
Most of the agenda is end-of-year student recognition. Item A honors 2015 All-State winter athletes, chiefly synchronized swimmers coached by Lori Uchwal, plus swimmer Zachary Chen and basketball player John Van Hoef. Item B recognizes the 2014-15 synchronized swimming state champions; Item C lists Senior Scholar Athletes with a 3.5 grade point average. Item D recognizes a Troy Education Association donation to the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, presented by TEA President Tony Lucchi to Foundation representative Rich Maziasz for the Tony Spagnola Memorial Golf Classic on June 19th. Items E through HHH cover academic and arts competitions across Bemis, Leonard and Wattles elementary schools, Baker, Boulan Park, Larson and Smith middle schools, Athens and Troy high schools and International Academy East, read by Mike Jolly, Nancy Philippart, Karl Schmidt, Paula Fleming, Ida Edmunds and Todd Miletti.

**Personnel (Item 6)**
New hire Kerry Collins, .6 FTE Resource Room Teacher at Athens High School, on a probationary contract for the remainder of the 2014-2015 school year. Jordan Harris, formerly a UniServ Director with the Michigan Education Association, is recommended as Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, effective August 3, 2015. Erica Rolack, most recently principal at Dixon Educational School in Detroit Public Schools, is recommended as Elementary Principal, effective July 1, 2015.

**Curriculum (Item 7)**
Adoption of the National Geographic Reach program (A, B, C levels) and the Grammar Gallery for ELD students in kindergarten through 5th grade, recommended May 5, 2015 by Elementary ELD Co-Chairpersons Christin Silagy and Danielle Andresen. Approval of a Michigan Council for Arts and Cultural Affairs grant to Troy High School that brought the Detroit Chamber Winds and Strings program to Troy High and Smith Middle School.

**Business (Item 8)**
A public hearing on the proposed 2015-2016 budget is set for June 23, 2015 at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098, with notice published at least six days in advance. The Administration and Services building roof replacement is awarded to J.D. Candler Roofing at $341,400.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, under 2013 Bond Series 1 Bid Package #14. The Sodexo Management, Inc. food service contract is renewed for 2015/2016, with a guarantee amount of $152,159. A point-of-sale system is awarded to Business Machine Company at $37,401.00 from the 2014-2015 Food Services Fund. Paid lunch prices rise $0.15 under Section 205 of the Healthy, Hunger-Free Kids Act of 2010:

| Lunch price | 2014-15 student | 2014-15 adult | 2015-16 student | 2015-16 adult |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| K-5 | $2.25 | $3.25 | $2.40 | $3.40 |
| 6-12 | $2.50 | $3.25 | $2.65 | $3.40 |
| 6-12 | $3.50 | $3.50 | $3.65 | $3.65 |
| 6-12 | $3.75 | $4.75 | $3.90 | $4.90 |

**Other (Item 10)**
Ron Curtis of Barton Malow gives a 2013 Bond Program Series 1 construction update covering Troy High School classroom and storage additions, the Athens High School LGI renovation, and Boulan Park and Larson office additions. The Board also considers revising the rest of the 2015 meeting schedule so workshops fall on the first Tuesday and regular meetings on the third Tuesday, beginning September 2015.

**Meeting and format**
Board Meeting Agenda for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of Tuesday, June 2, 2015 at 7:00 p.m. at Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085 -- an off-site location noted on the district calendar as "June 2, 2015 (location: Athens)." District headquarters is 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, telephone 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition -- Item 2, subitems A through HHH**
Item 2.A names the 2015 All-State winter athletes: synchronized swimmers Ellen Barker, Camille Bedford, Soumeeka Koneru, Kaylee Lee (2014 Colt of the Year), Julia Meng, Anjali Munasinghe, Daphne Samuel (2015 Colt of the Year), Hye-Kyung "Matilda" Seo (2015 Senior of the Year), Bhavya Sukhavasi, Amishi Taneja, Katie Ward and Christina Xu, all coached by Lori Uchwal; Zachary Chen (Senior, Troy High, boys swimming; All State 2015; school record for 200 Individual Medley; Coach Tom Buckheim); and John Van Hoef (Senior, Athens High, boys basketball; All State 2015 1st team; Academic All State; MVP Holiday Hoops Classic; Coach Dave Scott).
Item 2.B lists the 2014-15 Synchronized Swimming State Champions from Troy High and Athens High, including Monica Alluri, Priya Bandstra, Haya Beydoun, Michelle Cai, Inwoo Cho, June Choi, Joy Goldschmidt, Hanna Jung, Yejin Kim, Michelle Lebbos, Angela Li, Claire Li, Hemali Mistry, Anna Nichols, Jaclyn Anne Pabalan, Sabina Ravindran, Anisha Shukla, Sameeksha Venkatesh, Rohini Verma, Serena Yee and Kathleen Young, with Head Coach Lori Uchwal and assistants Katie Denning, Amanda Dine and Beth Borland. Item 2.C lists 2014-15 Senior Scholar Athletes carrying a 3.5 grade point average. Item 2.D recognizes the Troy Education Association for sponsoring a hole at the Tony Spagnola Memorial Golf Classic, the primary fundraiser for the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, held June 19th; TEA President Tony Lucchi presents the check to Foundation representative Rich Maziasz.
Items 2.E through 2.HHH honor competition results: an Athens student won Best in the State of Michigan/Best in Show at the DAFT Michigan Student Film Festival, in its 47th year, for "STEM Powered: Fostering Curiosity"; over 2,500 students competed at the State DECA Conference at the Amway Hotel in Grand Rapids; Destination Imagination Global Finals in May drew over 1,100 teams from 45 states, 7 Canadian provinces and 13 countries; an International Academy East Intel International Science and Engineering Fair entry (agenda-listed as Intel Science Talent Search) addressed "Self-Assembled Nanometer-sized Magnetic Sensors and Arrays for Bio-magnetic Imaging"; a Boulan Park student won the 19th Annual Jackie Robinson Art, Essay and Poetry Contest with a poem on "Courage"; Athens student Gloria took first in Michigan at the Japanese Speech Contest of March 28th at the Novi Civic Center, winning a $300 flight voucher; the Math Kangaroo Olympiad of March 19th drew 21,000 American students and over 6,000,000 worldwide; Larson Middle School reached "Emerald" status in Michigan Green Schools; nearly 22,000 students sat the National German Exam; the Baker Bobcats took 1st Place on May 1st in Road Scholar, Bottle Rocket and Picture This and finished 4th place among the top 48 qualifying Science Olympiad teams in Michigan, while Boulan Park fields 30 students across 23 events; Troy High's Symphonic Orchestra won the highest award at the National Festival in Florida; and in the USA Biology Olympiad 7,766 students took the exam nationwide, 12 Troy High semifinalists placed in the top 10%, and one reached finalist level (top 20 in the U.S.) and placed 6th in the National Biology Competition against over 4,000 students. Further items cover the Arctic Bookmark Contest, the American Mathematics Competitions (more than 350,000 students), Business Professionals of America, the Chemistry Olympiad, FIRST Robotics, HOSA, MATHCOUNTS, Math Madness, the Michigan Youth Arts Festival, MIT INSPIRE, the MSBOA All-State Band, the National French, Japanese, Spanish and Language Arts exams, Purple Comet, Robofest, the Siemens Competition and the WordMasters Challenge.

**Personnel -- Item 6**
6.A recommends a probationary contract for the remainder of the 2014-2015 school year for Kerry Collins, .6 FTE Resource Room Teacher at Athens High School. Her sketch lists a B.A. from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, May 2009 (major History, minor Psychology); an M.A. from Oakland University, Detroit, April 2012 (Special Education); a Michigan Professional Certificate in January 2015; Resource Room Teacher in the Waterford School District January 2013 to April 2015; Social Studies Teacher at Chandler Park Academy, Harper Woods, August 2010 to January 2013; and Guest Teacher in the Troy School District August 2009 to August 2010. Resident community: Shelby Township, Michigan.
6.B recommends Mr. Jordan Harris as Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services. He comes from the Michigan Education Association, where he spent the past 6 years as UniServ Director, first for Lansing Community College and then for Wayne County, and earlier spent 4 years as an attorney with Collins & Blaha, P.C. in Farmington Hills. He received his Juris Doctor in 2004 from the Michigan State University College of Law and his Master of Science in Labor Relations and Human Resources and Bachelor of Arts in International Relations from Michigan State University in 2003 and 2001. The resolution issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, with duties beginning August 3, 2015.
6.C recommends Ms. Erica Rolack as Elementary Principal (the agenda lists the position as Principal, Leonard Elementary School). She comes from Detroit Public Schools after 16 years there -- 6 years as a middle school teacher, 5 as an elementary teacher, one as an instructional specialist, 3 as an assistant principal and the past year as principal at Dixon Educational School. She earned a Bachelor's in Elementary Education from Wayne State University in 1999 and a Master's in Educational Psychology in 2007, and would begin July 1, 2015.

**Curriculum -- Item 7**
7.A adopts the elementary ELD materials recommended at the May 5, 2015 Board meeting by Elementary ELD Co-Chairpersons Christin Silagy and Danielle Andresen: the National Geographic Reach program (A, B, C levels) and the Grammar Gallery for ELD students in kindergarten through 5th grade, for 2015-2016. 7.B approves a Michigan Council for Arts and Cultural Affairs grant to Troy High School for a project that brought the Detroit Chamber Winds and Strings program to Troy High School and Smith Middle School through lectures, demonstrations and a shared concert.

**Business -- Item 8**
8.A sets a public hearing on the proposed 2015-2016 budget for June 23, 2015 at a regular Board meeting beginning at 7:00 p.m. at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098. Michigan law requires notice at least six (6) days beforehand, including in 11-point bold faced type the statement that the property tax millage rate proposed to be levied to support the proposed budget will be a subject of the hearing. Exhibit A, signed by Board Secretary Paula Fleming, states copies will be available at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., Wednesday, June 17, 2015 through Tuesday, June 23, 2015.
8.B awards the Administration and Services buildings roof replacement to J.D. Candler Roofing in the amount of $341,400.00, approved as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. Bids were reviewed by Mr. Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance and Operations, Mr. Ron Curtis of Barton Malow, and Ms. Michelle Kerns, Owners Representative. A Letter of Intent/Notice to Proceed dated May 20, 2015 from Douglas Madden, Sr. Project Manager, Barton Malow Company, is addressed to JD Candler, 31111 Industrial Drive, Livonia, MI 48150, under "2013 Bond Series 1 Bid Package #14, Administration & Services Building Roofing Replacement," directing shop drawings to Barton Malow Co and TMP Associates, with that cost reimbursed if the project were canceled on or before the award date of June 2nd, 2015. Contact: Doug Madden at (248) 219.4295; Central File: 104077.
8.C renews the food services contract with Sodexo Management, Inc. for the 2015/2016 school year; the Board approved the original contract resolution on May 6, 2014, and renewal requires annual approval by both the Michigan Department of Education and the Troy Board of Education. Ruby Zavala, Departmental Analyst, Food Service Contracts, Child Nutrition Programs, MDE, PO Box 30008, Lansing MI 48909, emailed approval of the FSMC renewal on Tuesday, May 26, 2015 at 8:19 AM, copying Katherine Fuller; Rick West forwarded it at 9:57:10 AM to Patricia R Orczykowski, copying Gayle M Moran. West's May 6, 2015 letter to Cheryl Schubel of MDE lists the RFP adjustments: a Meal Equivalent Factor for 2015-2016 of $3.2300; an administration fee rising from $0.13 in 2014-15 to $0.1339 in 2015-16, an increase of 3.0%; a management fee rising from $0.119 to $0.1225, an increase of 3.0%; a guarantee amount for 2015-2016 of $152,159, subject to adjustment for legislation such as the Healthy, Hunger-Free Kids Act of 2010; and no capital equipment planned for FSMC purchase in 2015/16.
8.D awards the Point of Sale System contract to Business Machine Company in the amount of $37,401.00 as an expenditure of the 2014-2015 Food Services Fund. Bids were reviewed by Kris Young, Director of Technology; Gayle Moran, General Manager, Sodexo Food Services; and John Foster, Convergent Technology Partners. Moran's May 6, 2015 memo on BID 9809 -- Food Service POS Equipment states the specification was to furnish and deliver 39 Point of Sale units for the School Lunch Program and that invitations to bid went to seven potential bidders. The 5/28/2015 bid tabulation reads:

| Vendor | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Business Machines Company | $37,401.00 |
| Crimson Solutions, LLC | $37,245.00 (alternate bid of $29,250, not to spec) |
| Food Service Solutions, Inc. | $35,061.00 |
| Heartland Payment Solutions, Inc. | $58,890.00 |
| Scan Technology, Inc. | $46,761.00 (alternate bid of $35,841, not to spec) |
| TekVisions, Inc. | $34,203.00 |

8.E adopts a paid lunch price adjustment required by Section 205 of the Healthy, Hunger-Free Kids Act of 2010, using the paid lunch equity (PLE) tool from the USDA Food and Nutrition Service. Rick West's May 21, 2015 memo to Superintendent Dr. Rich Machesky states that Troy's calculation yields a weighted average price of $2.55 against a 2015-16 weighted average requirement of $2.70, so a $0.15 increase per paid lunch is recommended:

| Lunch price | 2014-15 student | 2014-15 adult | 2015-16 student | 2015-16 adult |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| K-5 | $2.25 | $3.25 | $2.40 | $3.40 |
| 6-12 | $2.50 | $3.25 | $2.65 | $3.40 |
| 6-12 | $3.50 | $3.50 | $3.65 | $3.65 |
| 6-12 | $3.75 | $4.75 | $3.90 | $4.90 |

The attached PLE worksheets show a SY 2015-16 weighted average price requirement of $2.70 (also $2.70 rounded down to the nearest 5 cents), a SY 2014-15 unrounded price requirement of $2.62, and a note that prices are based on adjusting the SY 2014-2015 requirement by the 2% rate increase plus the Consumer Price Index (2.19%). The October 2014 price calculator lists 34,481 paid lunches at $2.25 generating $77,582.25; 16,134 at $2.50 generating $40,335.00; 9,942 at $3.50 generating $34,797.00; and 1,169 at $3.75 generating $4,383.75, totaling 61,726 lunches and $157,098.00 of monthly revenue at a weighted average price of $2.55. The optional estimation block uses the same counts at $2.50, $2.75, $3.75 and $4.00 to produce $86,202.50, $44,368.50, $37,282.50 and $4,676.00, a total of $172,529.50 and a weighted average price of $2.80. The sheet records a total price increase for SY 2015-16 of $0.15, a remaining increase carried forward to SY 2016-17 of $0.05, and figures of $2.65 and a 10 cent cap on the required price increase line.

**Other -- Item 10**
10.A is a report requiring no action by Ron Curtis, Senior Project Manager from Barton Malow, on the 2013 Bond Program Series 1 construction update dated 6.2.15, prepared by Barton Malow | TMP. Troy High School classroom and storage additions and the Boulan Park and Larson office additions carry completion dates of approximately December 2015; Troy Athens High School's LGI and multi-use classroom renovation is listed for Spring 2015. Planned 2015 projects: BP #8, Athens High School mechanical and electrical upgrades, out for bids August 2015; BP #9, Larson and Boulan Park mechanical and electrical upgrades and site paving, contracts awarded; BP #14, Administration & Service Center roofing, bids received May 13, 2015; BP #15, Costello and Wass elementary roofing; BP #16, Hamilton Elementary doors, flooring and mechanical and electrical upgrades; and BP #17, International Academy East, converting the pool to an LGI room and replacing doors and windows -- the last three out for bids December 2015.
10.B asks the Board to revise its meeting schedule for the remainder of the 2015 calendar year so that workshops fall on the first Tuesday of each month followed by regular Board meetings on the third Tuesday, beginning in September 2015. The attached calendar, dated 01.13.15, shows regular meetings at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, at 7:00 p.m. on January 13 (Organizational & Regular Meeting), February 3, March 3, April 14, May 5, June 2 (location: Athens), June 16, July 7 and August 4, 2015, with the fall dates overstruck and revised to September 15, October 20, November 17 and December 15, 2015 and January 19, 2016. Workshops at the Administrative Center, 4400 Livernois, at 6:00 p.m. run January 20, a Winter Retreat Saturday, January 24 at 9:30 a.m., February 10, March 17, April 21, May 19 and June 9, 2015, with fall workshops revised to September 1, October 6, November 10 and December 1, 2015.

The agenda carries three personnel items — administrative appointments of Kristine Griffor as Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction and Christin Silagy as Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments, both effective July 1, 2015 — plus ratification of a one-year successor agreement with the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA. **Meeting**
Agenda of Special Meeting, Troy Board of Education, June 16, 2015, 5:30 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, phone 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools; district site www.troy.k12.mi.us. Consent agenda items are acted on at one time unless removed.

**Agenda order**
1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Personnel (A. Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction; B. Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments; C. TESPA Contract Ratification); 4. Closed Session (A. Superintendent Evaluation); 5. Adjournment.

**3.A — Administrative Appointment: Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction**
Recommendation of Ms. Kristine Griffor. She comes to Troy from Warren Woods Public Schools, where she spent the past 8 years — first as an Intervention Specialist for 3 years, then 5 years as Director of Curriculum. Before Warren Woods she spent 4 years as an English Language Arts teacher for Richmond Community Schools. Oakland University degrees: Bachelor's in teaching (2003), Master's in Reading Instruction (2005), Educational Specialist in Educational Leadership (2007). The suggested resolution issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position, with duties beginning July 1, 2015.

**3.B — Administrative Appointment: Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments**
Recommendation of Ms. Christin Silagy. She joined the Troy School District in 2001 from Burbank Unified School District in Burbank, California, where she was a fourth grade teacher for 2 years. In 14 years with Troy she taught Science, Language Arts and English as a Second Language at Baker Middle School for 2 years, then moved to Bemis and Schroeder Elementary Schools as Program for Accelerated and Creative Education Resource Teacher for a year, and in 2004 moved to Morse Elementary School, where she currently serves as Elementary ELD Coordinator. Oakland University degrees: Bachelor's in Elementary Education (1999), Master's in Curriculum, Instruction and Leadership (2003), Educational Specialist in School Administration (2005). Duties begin July 1, 2015.

**3.C — TESPA Contract Ratification**
Tentative agreement reached June 5, 2015 between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA (TESPA), whose membership comprises paraprofessionals and skilled-trades employees. Membership ratified on June 10, 2015. Term: one year, July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2016.

| Economic term | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Salary schedule | 1% across-the-Board increase, including longevity steps |
| Steps | Step movement for all eligible members |
| Off-schedule | 4% payment to tier 1 schedule members (hired prior to February 14, 2012) currently on step 5 or higher |
| Life insurance | Premium cost for an additional $20,000 in coverage for the 5 skilled trade employees |
| Work boots | $200 reimbursement for the 5 skilled trade employees |
| Stated net increase | Approximately $30,000 in new dollars over 2014/15; characterized as less than 1.5% |

A supporting memorandum dated Friday, June 12, 2015 from Larry Lobert, Interim Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services, and Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, to Dr. Rich Machesky and the Board notes that part of the increase is retained as off-schedule (non-compounding) payments, and that the agreement states such payments are for 2015/16 only and are not a basis or starting point for a successor contract — preserving flexibility if the district's financial condition requires modifications. Attachments: signed Tentative Agreement and Board Resolution. Remaining language changes are described as without significant monetary impact.

**4.A — Closed Session**
Resolution to go into closed session to discuss the Superintendent Evaluation, as permitted by the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c). No additional business follows other than adjournment. Roll call vote lines: Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.verbose:
Board of Education agenda packet for a special meeting of the Troy School District held Tuesday, June 16, 2015 at 5:30 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248.823.4000). The standard header notes that district information is available at www.troy.k12.mi.us, that Board of Education meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and that meetings can also be viewed online at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The notice states that subjects to be discussed, considered, or acted upon are listed below, that items do not have to be taken in the order shown, and that items identified within the consent agenda are acted on at one time unless removed.

AGENDA STRUCTURE. The five numbered items are: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Personnel — Elementary Instruction; Grants & State Assessments; (TESPA) Contract Ratification, itemized as A. Consideration: Administrative Appointment — Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction (packet page 2), B. Consideration: Administrative Appointment — Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments (packet page 11), and C. Consideration: Troy Educational Support Personnel Association (packet page 18); 4. Closed Session — A. Consideration: Superintendent Evaluation (packet page 22); and 5. Adjournment.

ITEM 3.A — ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, ASSISTANT SUPERINTENDENT, ELEMENTARY INSTRUCTION. The Superintendent recommends the appointment of Ms. Kristine Griffor to the position of Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction. Ms. Griffor comes to Troy from Warren Woods Public Schools, where she spent the past 8 years, serving first as an Intervention Specialist for 3 years and the remaining 5 years as Director of Curriculum. Prior to Warren Woods, Ms. Griffor spent 4 years as an English Language Arts teacher for Richmond Community Schools. She attended Oakland University, receiving her Bachelor's degree in teaching in 2003, her Master's degree in Reading Instruction in 2005, and her Educational Specialist degree in Educational Leadership in 2007. With Board approval, Ms. Griffor will begin her duties as Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction effective July 1, 2015. The recommended action is acceptance of a suggested resolution (with Moved by / Supported by and Yes / No lines) reading: BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the Board of Education issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Ms. Kristine Griffor, who will begin her duties as Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, effective July 1, 2015.

ITEM 3.B — ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, DIRECTOR OF ELD, FEDERAL GRANTS & STATE ASSESSMENTS. The Superintendent recommends the appointment of Ms. Christin Silagy to the position of Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments. Ms. Silagy came to the Troy School District in 2001 from the Burbank Unified School District in Burbank, California, where she served as a fourth grade teacher for 2 years. During her 14 years with Troy, Ms. Silagy taught Science, Language Arts and English as a Second Language at Baker Middle School for 2 years. She then moved to Bemis and Schroeder Elementary Schools as the Program for Accelerated and Creative Education Resource Teacher for a year. In 2004 she moved to Morse Elementary School, where she currently serves as an Elementary ELD Coordinator. Ms. Silagy attended Oakland University, receiving her Bachelor's degree in Elementary Education in 1999, her Master's degree in Curriculum, Instruction and Leadership in 2003, and her Educational Specialist degree in School Administration in 2005. With Board approval, she will begin her duties as Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments as of July 1, 2015. The suggested resolution states that the Board of Education takes action to approve the aforementioned personnel recommendation as stated above, with Moved by / Supported by and Yes / No lines.

ITEM 3.C — TESPA CONTRACT RATIFICATION. A tentative agreement between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA (TESPA) was reached on June 5, 2015. The TESPA membership, comprised of paraprofessionals and skilled-trades employees, voted to ratify the agreement on June 10, 2015. The new one-year contract is for the period commencing July 1, 2015 and ending June 30, 2016. The agreement includes a 1% increase in the existing salary schedule, step movement for all eligible members, and a 4% off-schedule payment to members on the tier 1 schedule who are currently on step 5 or higher. The agreement also includes additional language changes that do not have significant monetary impact. The suggested resolution states that the Board of Education hereby ratifies and adopts the tentative agreement reached on June 5, 2015 between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA for the period of July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2016, with Moved by / Supported by and Yes / No lines.

SUPPORTING MEMORANDUM ON THE TESPA TENTATIVE AGREEMENT. A memorandum dated Friday, June 12, 2015 is addressed to Dr. Rich Machesky, Superintendent, and the Board of Education, from Larry Lobert, Interim Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services, and Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, regarding the TESPA Tentative Agreement. Contact details shown on the memorandum are the Business Office, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, phone 248.823.4022 and fax 248.823.4013. The memorandum announces that a tentative agreement has been reached with TESPA and that it is recommended for Board action at the June 16, 2015 meeting since member ratification has occurred. It states the agreement allows for a net increase (new dollars over 2014/2015) of less than 1.5%, attributed to changes in the pay structure explained in the memorandum and outlined in the attached signed Tentative Agreement. The agreement is described as providing modest improvements to the salary structure while retaining portions of the increase as off-schedule (non-compounding) payments; a clear understanding is expressed in the agreement that such payments are for 2015/16 only and are not to be considered as a basis or starting point for a successor contract, which the memorandum says will help the district retain some flexibility if the district's financial condition requires modifications next year.

The memorandum states the total dollar net increase over 2014/15 is approximately $30,000, comprising the following economics: a 1% across-the-Board increase to the existing salary schedule, including longevity steps; step movement for all eligible members; a 4% off-schedule payment for employees on the tier 1 schedule (those hired prior to February 14, 2012) who are currently on step 5 or higher; premium costs for an additional $20,000 in life insurance coverage for the 5 skilled trade employees; and a $200 reimbursement for work boots for the 5 skilled trade employees. Readers are directed to contact either Larry Lobert or Rick West with questions, comments, or concerns. Attachments listed are the signed Tentative Agreement and the Board Resolution.

ITEM 4.A — CLOSED SESSION, SUPERINTENDENT EVALUATION. The packet notes the Board must pass a resolution to go into closed session to discuss the Superintendent Evaluation, and that following passage of the resolution the Board of Education will go into closed session, after which no additional business will take place other than to officially adjourn the meeting. The recommended action is adoption of a resolution stating that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), the Troy Board of Education shall go into closed session to discuss Superintendent Evaluation. A roll call vote is required, with named lines for Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, and Fleming. The agenda concludes with item 5, Adjournment.

**Personnel items.** Item 7.A appoints Ms. Jennifer Gottlieb as Director of Student Growth, Equity & Assessment effective July 1, 2015 on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure; she returns from Macomb Intermediate School District, where she was Science Consultant for two years, after two years as Science Coordinator with Birmingham Public Schools and fifteen years with Troy Schools (three as Science and Math Coordinator, twelve teaching science at Athens High School), with degrees from the University of Michigan (1989), Columbia University's Teachers College (1990) and Oakland University (Education Specialist, 2011). Item 7.B reports Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky's first-year evaluation as HIGHLY EFFECTIVE, crediting him with launching One Troy and negotiating all labor contracts; the Board authorized a $5,000 bonus and a 3.5% base salary increase and extended his contract from July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2017 without tenure. Item 7.C extends Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, and Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning, through June 30, 2017, the narrative describing the action inconsistently as one-year extensions and as two-year successor contracts, with current contracts said to expire June 30, 2016. Goss, Dan House, William Turner, Amy Buchanan, Jonathan Cross, Diane Kocenda, Anthony Morse, Kerry Birmingham, Rob Carson, Michael Jolly, Stephanie Maynard, Kris Young, John Schiesler and Shawna Veit. Item 7.E ratifies a one-year agreement with the Troy Educational Secretaries Association/MEA/NEA for July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2016, tentatively agreed June 18, 2015 and ratified June 22, 2015: a 2% across-the-board wage-schedule improvement, two step movements on the 21-step schedule, a 3% off-schedule payment for those not benefiting from step movement, elimination of the $100/$200 health insurance premium deductible payments in Appendix 16 of the 13/15 agreement, and elimination of the former 4% off-schedule payment.

**Business items.** Item 9.A approves an Operating Millage Proposal for a Special School Election on November 3, 2015, conducted by the Clerk of the County of Oakland and certified to the Election Coordinator on or before August 11, 2015 under Michigan Election Law (Public Act 116 of 1954). The ballot asks 18.3795 mills against all property except principal residences, with 18 mills the maximum allowable levy ($18.00 per $1,000 of taxable valuation), and 5.99 mills against principal residences ($5.99 per $1,000), both for nine years, 2016 to 2025 inclusive; 17.8795 of the 18.3795 mills and the 5.99 mills renew authority expiring December 31, 2015, while 0.1205 mills restores millage lost to the Michigan Constitution's required reduction. Estimated revenue is $33,583,000 during calendar 2016; Paula Fleming, Board Secretary, certifies the resolution. Item 9.B adopts the 2014-15 budget amendment: $145,113,344 General Fund, $8,406,495 Special Revenue, $54,664,295 Debt Service, $19,434,618 2014 Capital Projects and $101,800 Capital Maintenance. General Fund revenue is amended from $142,706,181 to $142,113,297 and expenditures from $143,627,633 to $145,113,344, moving the projected result from $(921,452) to $(3,000,047) and the June 30 fund balance from $20,458,563 to $18,379,968. Item 9.C adopts the 2015-16 appropriations: General Fund $137,945,141 (one resolved clause prints $140,945,141), Special Revenue $7,795,216, Debt Service $16,588,938, 2014 Capital Projects $98,866,705 and Capital Maintenance $0. General Fund revenue is $136,512,079 (local $35,198,639, state $90,070,344, federal $3,395,503, transfers and other $7,847,593) against a July 1, 2015 balance of $18,379,968 for $154,892,047 available, with total instruction $92,744,689, total support services $45,123,193 and community services $77,259. Millage rates approved are 17.8795 mills non-homestead, 10.9918 mills commercial personal property, 4.9918 mills homestead and industrial personal property, and 4.70 mills on all classes for debt retirement. Debt Service revenue is $16,650,931 against $11,660,000 of principal, $4,922,738 of interest and $6,200 of other expenses; the 2014 Capital Projects Fund anticipates $67,489,416 of bond proceeds and $97,377,710 of capital outlay; Capital Maintenance appropriates $0 against a $701,919 balance. Item 9.D awards Roof Assessment and Consulting Services, reviewed by Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance and Operations, and owner's representative Michelle Kerns, to WeatherTech Consulting Group, Inc. for $99,128.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. Item 11.A closes with a 2014/2015 School Year in Review video.
